title: Understanding Fieldtypes
excerpt: Explore the various fieldtypes available in HaruCMS and how to use them effectively. From text fields to rich content editors, learn what each type offers.
content:
Fieldtypes are the building blocks of your content structure in HaruCMS. Each fieldtype is designed for a specific type of data, making it easier to create, manage, and validate your content. Understanding which fieldtype to use for each piece of information is crucial for building an effective content model.

Text Fieldtypes

Text

The basic text fieldtype is perfect for single-line inputs like titles, names, or short identifiers. It's simple, fast, and ideal for metadata that doesn't require formatting.

Textarea

Use textarea fields for longer, unformatted text like excerpts, descriptions, or code snippets. Unlike rich text fields, textareas preserve plain text formatting, making them perfect for content that needs to be displayed exactly as entered.

Rich Content Fieldtypes

Rich Text

The rich text editor provides a full WYSIWYG experience for formatted content. Perfect for blog posts, articles, and any content that needs headings, lists, links, and other formatting. The editor includes formatting toolbar with options for bold, italic, links, lists, and more.

Media Fieldtypes

Media

The media fieldtype handles file uploads and image management. You can upload images, documents, or other files, and the system automatically generates thumbnails for images. The media manager lets you organize and reuse uploaded files across entries.

Structured Data Fieldtypes

Tags

Tag fields allow you to add multiple keywords or labels to your content. Tags are great for categorization, filtering, and organizing content. The tag field supports autocomplete, making it easy to reuse existing tags and maintain consistency.

Select

Select fields provide dropdown menus with predefined options. Use them for categories, statuses, or any field with a limited set of possible values. This ensures data consistency and makes filtering easier.

Advanced Fieldtypes

Relation

The relation fieldtype lets you link entries together, creating relationships between different pieces of content. For example, you might link blog posts to authors, or products to categories. This creates a flexible, interconnected content structure.

Choosing the Right Fieldtype

When designing your content schema, consider:

  • Data type: What kind of information are you storing?
  • Length: Will it be short (text) or long (textarea/rich text)?
  • Formatting: Does it need formatting (rich text) or should it be plain (textarea)?
  • Structure: Is it a single value (text) or multiple values (tags)?
  • Relationships: Does it need to link to other content (relation)?

By choosing the right fieldtype for each piece of content, you create a structure that's both easy to use and powerful enough to handle complex content needs.
